title: Paul Nicholas: Musicals Marigolds & Me - review
transcript: hello and welcome to one-minute theater reviews i'm paul seven-lewis and if you're fascinated by show business then i think you'll be interested in this new autobiography by paul nicholas called musicals marigolds and me he's already given us one slice of his life back in 1999 so his latest contribution concentrates on his career as opposed to his personal life and in particular brings us up to date with his 21st century life as a producer touring in musicals and his newfound stardom as one of the inhabitants of tv's real marigold hotel and since this latter is what many people now know him for paul sensibly starts with a few stories about his experiences on the tv program and very amusing they are too i haven't seen the show but this did tempt me to watch it the most interesting part of the book for me anyway is the behind the scenes story of what it's like to be a producer in particular his contribution to his greatest successes greece and saturday night fever during my time in theater management i worked with paul on a number of occasions and his book is very like himself he rarely boasts he doesn't upset anybody and he keeps most of his life private and in a way this is where the book falls down a bit you get very little sense of what it feels like to be a star or to be in the middle of the world of show business well that's my one minute review keep watching for more about paul nicholas's autobiography musicals marigolds and me the book starts with a lot about the real marigold hotel tv series and i think this will please the show's many fans as i said i haven't watched it so it wasn't so interesting for me um i got more interested when he went on to talk about his career in show business and after the many little stories about making the marigold programs i was disappointed that there were actually very few anecdotes about the rest of his career and when he does come up with a story he doesn't exaggerate or accommodate to make them more memorable and he certainly doesn't reveal any secrets sticking religiously to the unwritten rule that what happens backstage stays backstage i mean i'm not saying i was looking for juicy scandals and salacious gossip but just some colorful stories about the people and things that happened behind the scenes we learned about his early venture into the world of pop music which included some chart hits and touring with the likes of screaming lord such del shannon and the who but i mean how can you tour with a group as outrageous as the who and not have a story or two and has he really nothing to report on meeting david bowie beyond he didn't strike me as a happy-go-lucky person and this aspect of the book doesn't get any better when he embarks on his lengthy career as a musicals performer which included starring roles in the original productions of jesus christ superstar and cats really this section of the book reads like a wikipedia entry of i did this then i did that i met this person then i met that person well okay so you may not get much feeling for what the life or even the people were like but you do see how show business works and he shares some of what he's learned for example if you try to shortchange the public they will catch you out it's when he gets into producing that the book goes up a gear he's rightly proud of his achievement in this field including two outstanding west end musicals greece and saturday night fever it started in 1990 when he teamed up with david ian another very nice man to put together a touring production of the joseph pat version of the pirates of penzance we learn an awful lot about the difficulties of raising money casting and marketing for instance i never knew that it was paul who was responsible for that iconic greece logo when he had the idea of reviving greece in 1993 he dumped the original theater show and transformed it into a stage version of the film by incorporating new songs that are featured in the movie it proved immensely popular particularly with young people and then he moved on to producing the first stage version of saturday night fever and the details of his contribution to making the show the success it was from the original idea to stage the show the negotiations with robert stigwood who earned the rights the rewriting of the script more than once the discovery and training of the leading man adam garcia and the difficult decision to invest his own money will fascinate anyone who's interested in the business side of show business after his success as a co-producer of saturday night fever in the west end it's clear he was annoyed that robert stigward who held the rights went on to produce the show on broadway without him but he continues to praise him and reveals nothing nasty about the great man i think part of the reason may be that paul is a very nice man and who genuinely doesn't want to be unkind to anybody one thing that emerges very clearly from this book is the basis of his success he is of course talented but then so are many entertainers and he's certainly good looking and charming which helps and he was a born singer but he had to learn to act and to dance and he was never the greatest at any of these but what he did do was work hard at them he's the supreme example of the saying that success is one percent inspiration and 99 perspiration and as you'll find out in the book his work rate is hugely impressive i mean for singing in the reign he had to learn to dance well enough to play a role made famous by gene kelly and when he starred as barnum he had to learn juggling unicycling trampolining and tightrope walking he certainly deserves his success paul has a gentle sense of humor as when he says that even as an old man he still has fans although now quite elderly including a stalker i just have to walk very slowly he says and that's typical of paul it's no surprise that he's growing old gracefully i didn't of determination and hard work he's achieved a great deal but all with good grace and self-effacement and that's what you get in his latest autobiography i give musicals marigolds and me three stars i hope you found this review useful and if you want to be the first to know when i post a new review please subscribe to my channel one minute theater reviews thank you for watching
